title: Noah and Buttons Pull the Wagon
markdown:
Ranger Tess asked Noah the nest helper and Buttons the bear cub to move a heavy wagon full of books to her reading spot under the Whispering Willow.

Buttons, a fluffy bear cub, nudged the wagon. Rumble, creak. It barely wiggled. He pushed with all his might. Noah, a little bird, added his tiny weight. Still no luck.

“It’s too heavy to push!” sighed Buttons.

Noah watched a tiny ant try to move a big leaf. The ant pushed, but the leaf just sat there. Then the ant scurried to the other side and gave a mighty pull. The leaf slid.

“Pulling!” Noah chirped, eyes wide. “Buttons, let’s pull the wagon!”

Buttons tilted his head. “Pull, not push?”

“Yes!” Noah fluttered back. They found a strong vine. Noah tied one end to the wagon. Buttons grabbed the other end.

“Ready?” Noah chirped.

“Ready!” Buttons rumbled.

“One… two… THREE!”

They pulled together. Noah tugged, and Buttons heaved. The rope tightened. Buttons felt a strong tug in his paws. The wheels rumbled on the grass, and the wagon slid smoothly along. They pulled it all the way to the Whispering Willow.

Ranger Tess smiled. “You did it! How did you move such a heavy wagon?”

“We couldn’t push it,” said Buttons proudly. “But we learned to pull!”

Ranger Tess knelt. “The vine let you both pull the same way, and the wheels rolled with you. Pulling with a rope can move a load that a shove cannot.”

Noah and Buttons beamed. The books sat safe in the shade. Buttons shook out his paws. Noah hopped onto the wagon rim, and the vine, still tied, hung ready for the next trip.
characters: Noah (nest helper), Buttons (bear cub), Ranger Tess (ranger)
